A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SPE-BR pricing research and contain complete, readable main text and Appendices A–L. Text, equations, tables and graphics support a reliable comparison without material evidence gaps.

before.justification: v4.pdf reports original simulations in Section 6 and Appendix J, including estimation errors, Nash-equilibrium convergence and cumulative regret in Figures 5–8.

after.justification: v6.pdf retains these original simulation outcomes in Section 6 and Appendix J, including experiments with unequal exploration lengths and misspecified shape parameters.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 and Equations (10)–(12) retain the same parameter estimation, shape-constrained link estimation and subsequent best-response pricing procedure. No method component changes.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same synthetic markets with 2, 4 and 6 sellers, contraction regimes, unequal exploration lengths and shape misspecification. The new collusion discussion does not introduce an evaluated scenario.

E2.justification: The same algorithm variants and parameter regimes are compared. Neither version adds an experimentally evaluated external pricing baseline; comparisons with prior methods remain theoretical.

E3.justification: Section 6 and Appendix J retain the same horizons, price domain, demand functions, noise, exploration allocations and evaluation metrics. The protocols for unequal exploration lengths and shape misspecification also match.

E4.justification: Appendices J.1–J.3 retain the same contraction sensitivity, unequal-exploration robustness and shape-misspecification analyses, with unchanged Figures 5–8. Remark 5.8 adds interpretation without a collusion test.

E5.justification: Both versions report 30 independent simulation repetitions, averages and 95% confidence intervals in Section 6 and Appendix J. No run-count, seed or uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: The plotted results, fitted slopes and empirical findings in Figures 5–8 are unchanged. For example, Figure 8 retains equilibrium-convergence slope -0.34 and regret slope 0.56 for the unmisspecified shape setting.

T1.justification: The mathematical statements, assumptions, equations and appendix proofs are unchanged. Corrections such as 'Theorem 3.2' to 'Assumption 3.2' repair references to statements already correctly labeled in v4; they do not revise the theory.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution summary retain the same semiparametric pricing, equilibrium, regret and concentration claims. The new collusion remark is not incorporated into the headline contributions.

C2.justification: New Remark 5.8 interprets convergence under the shared algorithm as preventing collusion and coordinated price increases, claims a consumer benefit, and cautions that different learning rules may permit collusion. Existing interpretations and limitations remain.

D1.justification: Implementation and simulation details are retained. Both reproducibility statements describe the same supplementary ZIP archive, notebooks and instructions for regenerating plots; no access information or technical disclosures are added.

R1.justification: The cited works and positioning relative to competitive pricing, single-index models and shape-constrained estimation are unchanged. Bibliographic entries reflow across pages without additions or removals.

P1.justification: v6 systematically corrects reference types, including assumption, proposition, lemma and remark references, and replaces references to appendix 'sections' with 'Appendix'. Apart from the short new Remark 5.8, the narrative and section sequence remain.

P2.justification: v6 adds the ICLR 2026 publication header and changes top spacing, producing local text and display shifts. Existing figures and tables retain their graphics, structure, axes, legends and captions.

improvement.justification: Correcting misleading cross-references throughout the theory and appendices provides a modest net improvement in clarity and navigation. The scientific evidence is unchanged. Remark 5.8 adds a scope qualification, although its broad claim about preventing price increases is not separately established by the convergence result or simulations, limiting the gain.
